analysis.investment_thesis: Belrise is a capital-intensive auto ancillary growing revenues at 15% but earnings at only 10.7%, yielding a disqualifying PEG of ~3.7x — you're paying a fast-grower price for stalwart-grade earnings growth. With negative free cash flow in 2025 (-₹163 Cr) and operating margins of just 8.3%, this is a classic "hot IPO" trap I'd walk right past.
key_strengths: Revenue growing 15.4% CAGR, riding India's structural 2-wheeler boom with large OEM customers
Conservative balance sheet with D/E of just 0.29 and strong promoter backing at 66.46%
Diversifying into EV components (hub motors, battery containers) — optionality on India's EV transition
key_risks: PEG ratio of ~3.7x (P/E 39.6 ÷ EPS growth 10.7%) — wildly overpriced for the actual earnings growth delivered
Profit growth stalled in FY24 (₹314 Cr flat vs FY23's ₹314 Cr) despite 14% revenue growth — margins are being squeezed
Capex surge to ₹868 Cr in FY25 turned FCF deeply negative (-₹163 Cr); finance costs compound at 12.4% CAGR, eroding bottom line
red_flags: Recent IPO with equity nearly doubling (₹2,340→₹4,971 Cr) via capital raise — Lynch's rule: 'IPO = It's Probably Overpriced'
Operating margin only 8.3% in a commoditized, OEM-dependent business with limited pricing power
Net profit CAGR of 10.7% is half the revenue CAGR of 15.4% — operating leverage is running in reverse
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Belrise is an auto ancillary supplying 2W/3W/4W OEMs — a business I'd classify as a stalwart at best, and a cyclical at worst. The story isn't bad: India's 2-wheeler market is enormous, the company has real scale at ₹8,291 Cr revenue, and the EV component optionality is interesting. But the numbers don't support the price. A P/E of 39.6x on a business compounding earnings at only 10.7% gives a PEG of 3.7x — I want PEG under 1.0 and get nervous above 1.5. At nearly 4x, I'm paying a premium the growth simply doesn't justify.

What really bothers me is the disconnect between revenue and profit growth — revenue grew 53% over three years while net profit grew 35%, meaning margins are being consumed by rising finance costs (12.4% CAGR) and capex. FY25's ₹868 Cr capex against ₹704 Cr operating cash flow means the business burned ₹163 Cr of free cash. That's fine if you're building for a 10-bagger, but at 8.3% operating margins in a price-sensitive OEM supply chain, I don't see the path to dramatic margin expansion. The forward P/E of 27.6x implies the market is baking in ~43% earnings growth next year — heroic expectations for a company that just went public and historically grows earnings at 10%. Pass.
